disposition: The hello header rule now includes bounds == BoundedContext::none(); a hello frame with any nonzero bounds field is refused PROTOCOL_FRAME_INVALID (40001) by decode_frame, decode_frame_for_version and ProtocolFrame::validate_header, before the hello record is read (SMP1 revision 16 erratum, 2.0.1). The encoder is unchanged. The independent oracle (scripts/check_smp1_vector.py) now decodes the ProtocolFrame record and applies the same header rules; it had inspected only the envelope and accepted the frame. Pinned by the conformance rejection hello-nonzero-bounds (conformance/smp1/v1/rejected.json, byte-equal to the lane-0 minimized input without its lane byte), hello_frame_with_nonzero_bounds_is_refused_s20_700_smp1_002 (sley-protocol) and a_hello_frame_with_nonzero_bounds_is_refused_at_the_handshake (sley-cli). Both inputs are permanent corpus seeds and are retested on every smoke.
expected: The smp1_frame_decoder target completes without panic on both inputs: decode_frame refuses the frame with PROTOCOL_FRAME_INVALID, which is in ProtocolErrorCode::ALL, so the Err arm holds and nothing is re-encoded.
root_cause: sley-protocol accepted a non-canonical hello frame. ProtocolFrame::validate_for_version held a kind-4 frame to session None, request_id 0, method 0 and flags 0 but never checked its bounds, and decode_frame returns DecodedFrame::Hello with only the hello record, so a hello frame whose BoundedContext was not the all-zero context decoded, the bounds were dropped, and encode_hello_frame re-emitted zero bounds. The crash input is the accepted fixture server hello (seed S20-700-SMP1-001) with one byte changed: input byte 82 (frame byte 81), the one-byte value of bounds.applied_limits.max_frame_bytes, is 0x08 instead of 0x00; lane 1 rewrites the trailer, so the frame reaches the record rules and decodes. check_frame then failed 're-encoding a decoded frame drifted' at targets/smp1_frame_decoder.rs:101. Present in v2.0.0 (1fea02f).
